What the differences mean

  • Sony PS-LX3BT vs AT-LP70XBT: $399.99 − $299 = $100.99 more for the Sony. Turntableverse lists the same codecs for both (SBC, aptX, aptX Adaptive).
  • AT-LP70XBT vs AT-LP60XBT: $299 − $259 = $40 more gets you RCA outputs and a VM95-series stylus upgrade path, instead of a fixed ATN3600L and a 3.5 mm output.
  • AT-LP3XBT vs AT-LP70XBT: $379 − $299 = $80 more gets you an adjustable counterweight, anti-skate and a removable headshell, so you can fit any cartridge later.
  • Kanto OBI3 Gen 2 vs AT-LP60XBT: $259 − $249.99 = $9.01 less for the Kanto, but you lower the arm by hand.
  • Tracking force: HIFI.DE's Bernhard Rietschel measured 2.1 g on the AT-LP70XBT and 3.7 g on the PS-LX3BT. 3.7 ÷ 2.1 = 1.76, so the Sony presses on the groove about 76% harder.

Bluetooth to Sonos: which speakers take a turntable

Every deck above sends Bluetooth out to a speaker or headphones. Whether that works with Sonos depends on the speaker. Sonos lists these products as able to share Bluetooth audio with the rest of a Sonos system: Arc Ultra, Beam Ultra, Era 100, Era 100 SL, Era 300, Move 2, Roam, Roam 2, Roam SL and Sonos Play. The original Move is not on the list.

  • The speaker has to be set up on your Sonos system over WiFi first. Then group it from the Grouping menu, and it plays the turntable in the other rooms for as long as it stays grouped.
  • Sonos turns Bluetooth off on supported portable speakers while they are set up as surrounds.
  • Sonos says Roam, Sonos Ace and Sonos Ace Ultra cannot swap Bluetooth audio to or from other Sonos products.

If your Sonos speaker isn't on that list, connect the turntable by cable. Sonos says Era 100, Era 300 and Move 2 need its Line-In Adapter plus an RCA to 3.5 mm cable. Five and Play:5 take an RCA to 3.5 mm cable straight into line-in. Amp and Port take an RCA cable into the input marked IN. The AT-LP70XBT, AT-LP3XBT and TEAC have RCA outputs and a built-in preamp you can switch, so they plug straight into any of these. The Sony's RCA cable is attached to the deck, and for that case Sonos says a Five needs an RCA to 3.5 mm adapter.

Not recommended

Sony PS-LX3BT at $399.99. It is one-button simple, but at Turntable Lab's price today it costs $100.99 more than the AT-LP70XBT for the same codec list (per Turntableverse). Its stylus is a built-in ATN3600L type with no VM95 upgrade path, and HIFI.DE measured 3.7 g of tracking force against 2.1 g on the Audio-Technica.
